correctness.rationale: The exact total weight calculation is 1-a+(a+3)=4. With incident sums -1 on A and 1+epsilon on B, the closed Kneser neighborhood identity W-s_i-s_j+2 f_ij yields values at least 1 on crossing pairs, at least 8 on internal A pairs and at least 2 on internal B pairs. Every negative crossing pair has a-2>=2 disjoint 2-labelled cycle neighbors. For restricted sharpness, weight w<=3 implies maximum degrees p+q<=w-1 and an edge-capacity inequality; the only possible w=3 equality pattern is a two-regular graph on B, but a missing B-edge then has closed sum -1. Both independent verification mechanisms pass in their stated finite ranges.

value.rationale: The 2023 exact value four at n=10 and upper bound five for all larger even Kneser orders leave a natural persistence question. A cycle together with three disjoint larger-block edges establishes a uniform weight-four construction for the whole previously unresolved even-order range, reducing an established upper bound on an infinite family. The exact restricted sharpness supplies a structural explanation of the parity obstruction and why a weight-three modification of this sign template cannot work. This is not a gratuitous improvement of a known exact scalar, and the larger-order unrestricted optimum remains explicitly open.
